name: What do Los Angeles pool fill-in permits usually require?

mainEntity.name: What documents or plan details are usually required for a Los Angeles pool fill-in permit?
mainEntity.text: What documents or plan details are usually required for a Los Angeles pool fill-in permit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Los Angeles-area pool fill-in permit packages often need more than a basic application. A city may request a dimensioned site plan or plot plan showing property lines, the existing pool or spa footprint, nearby structures, and the planned demolition or fill area. Depending on the jurisdiction, the package may also need drainage information, utility disconnect details, grading notes, and sometimes soils or compaction documentation. Pasadena’s published rules explicitly call for an accurate dimensioned site plan during plan review. The goal is to show the city exactly what will be removed, what will remain, and how the filled area will drain after completion. Homeowners should ask the contractor or designer what drawings are required before submitting anything. Incomplete plan sets are a common reason projects stall or get rejected.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permit applications for pool fill-in commonly require a site or plot plan showing the pool location, property lines, and nearby structures. Some cities also require drainage details, utility disconnect information, and inspection scheduling. Pasadena specifically asks for an accurate dimensioned site plan as part of plan review.
